data.text: Hi, yes, I'm calling because my internet has been really slow for the last couple of days and I'm not sure what's going on. I've tried unplugging things but nothing seems to help.
I'll help you get to the bottom of this. Let me start by pulling up your account and running some diagnostics on your connection.

results.title: Modem Reboot Procedure
results.snippet: Reboot the modem when the customer reports: - No internet connection despite modem appearing powered on - Very slow speeds that did not improve after router restart

results.title: Slow Internet Speeds Troubleshooting
results.snippet: 1. **Weak modem signal** — downstream signal below -7 dBmV or above +7 dBmV indicates line issues. 2. **WiFi interference or distance** — 2.4 GHz band congestion; customer too far from router. 3. **Peak-hour congestion** — shared neighbourhood node oversubscribed in the evenings (6–10 PM).

results.title: Device Compatibility — Approved Modems and Routers
results.snippet: Customers must use a modem on the ISP-approved list to receive full technical support. Unapproved modems may work but are not guaranteed to provision correctly or receive remote management commands (including `reboot_modem_remotely`).

results.title: DNS Issues Troubleshooting
results.snippet: - Websites fail to load but the customer can ping IP addresses directly (e.g., `ping 8.8.8.8` succeeds). - Browser shows "DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN" or "Server Not Found" errors. - Some websites work but others do not, seemingly at random.

results.title: WiFi vs. Ethernet — Troubleshooting Connectivity Differences
results.snippet: | Factor | Ethernet (wired) | WiFi (wireless) | |---|---|---| | Speed | Full subscribed tier | Up to 80% of tier (varies by band) |

data.text:
<analysis>
I've gathered the following diagnostic evidence:

**Customer Profile** [tool:lookup_customer]: Jane Smith, active account since 2021, Gigabit 500 service tier, NETGEAR CM500 modem + TP-Link Archer AX21 router, located in northeast (ZIP 10001).

**Modem Status** [tool:check_modem_status]: The modem is online but showing critical issues:
- Downstream signal at -12 dBmV (outside acceptable range; should be between -7 and +7 dBmV)
- Upstream signal at 44 dBmV (acceptable)
- **7 restarts in the last 24 hours** — indicates line instability
- Uptime only 0.5 hours (modem just restarted)
- Firmware V1.01.10

**Connectivity Test** [tool:ping_customer_modem]: High latency (287 ms) and 12.5% packet loss — consistent with signal degradation.

**ISP Outage Check** [tool:check_isp_outage]: No active outages in the customer's area.

**Knowledge Base** [kb:slow_speeds]: Weak downstream signal (below -7 dBmV) is a primary cause of slow speeds and indicates a line issue. The KB also notes that frequent restarts suggest line problems.

**Diagnosis**: This is a **line-quality issue**, not a WiFi or congestion problem. The weak downstream signal and frequent modem restarts point to a potential issue with the cable line itself — possibly a loose connection, signal splitter problem, or line degradation from the ISP's network to the customer's home. This requires a technician visit to inspect the physical line and connections.
</analysis>

<reply>
Jane, I've checked your modem and I can see what's causing the slowness. Your modem's signal is weaker than it should be, and it's been restarting multiple times a day — that's a sign of a line quality issue on our end. This isn't something a reboot will fix. I'd like to schedule a technician to come out and check your cable line and connections. Are you available for a visit in the next day or two?
</reply>
